style: Warm and unhurried, an old park ranger looking out over the valley.
lines: Welcome to the lookout. Tap a picture on the shelf to put it in the valley.
Drag it to move it. Pull the round corner to make it bigger or smaller.
Look at the side view. It shows how far away your picture says it is.
Size and place don't agree yet. Drag it up or down, or pull the round corner.
Solid. Now they agree.
Read the postcard's note. Drag and size things until every goal has a tick.
Tap the haystack, then tap Front.
Tap the hills, then tap Fade until they look misty.
It looks deep now. Tap Next postcard when you're ready.
Hogarth drew this picture full of mistakes on purpose. Tap something that looks wrong.
Look again. Try something that is too big or too small.
You found all eight. Every one breaks a rule of near and far.
Tap another mistake, or tap Whole picture to look again.
The valley is empty. Tap a picture on the shelf to begin again.
These pictures overlap. Tap Front or Back so the closer object covers the farther one.
One pine is near you. One pine is far away.
Make the fence run back into the distance.
The haystack is in front of the barn.
Three cows: one near, one in the middle, one far.
The fox is closest. The windmill is farthest. The round tree is in front of the barn.
The hills are far. The pine is near. Make the far things misty.
A sailboat is far out on the lake. Another is near the shore.
All the balloons fly at the same height. Put one near and one far.
Make size and place agree for both trees.
Far things are smaller and closer to the horizon.
Each post is as tall as your eyes. Its top touches the horizon.
Make each post to the right smaller and higher.
Move and size both until the Side View shows solid.
Move the haystack across part of the barn.
Tap the haystack, then Front.
The cow's back touches the horizon wherever she stands.
Make one big, one medium and one tiny. Move their backs to the horizon.
Each kind of object has its own height in this valley.
Use the Side View to compare distances.
Move the tree over part of the barn. Tap the tree, then Front.
Move the TOP of the hills to the horizon. Size the pine and barn to match their place.
Tap Fade: crisp under 40 m, soft 40 to 150 m, misty beyond 150 m.
Drag a boat. It stays on the water. Size it to match its place.
A far boat is small and very close to the horizon.
All baskets fly 40 m above the ground. Size and place must agree.
Up in the sky, far things are lower, closer to the horizon.
These sheep get bigger as they go farther away.
This bird is huge next to the tree it sits on.
The man on the far hill is taller than the trees.
The swan is bigger than the men in the boat.
The far trees are in front of the near sign.
The near fisherman's line goes behind the far fisherman's line.
The woman in a near window holds a candle up to a man on a far hill.
You can see the top and the bottom of this barrel at once.
Drag it again, or use Front, Back and Fade to change its depth cues.
Drag another object, or use Front, Back and Fade.
Almost. A little higher.
Almost. A little lower.
Drag to move it. Pull the round corner to change its size.
Tap another picture on the shelf to add it.
Progress cleared. Drag and size the pictures, or choose another postcard.
Drag a cow so its back meets the horizon.
Drag or size an object. Tap Show horizon to see your eye level again.
Your flat start becomes your deep postcard. Tap Before and after to look again.
Tap a mistake on the print, or tap Show me one.
Tap another mistake on the print, or tap Show me one.
Tap something too big or too small, or tap Show me one.
You found every mistake. Tap a marked spot to look again, or choose Valley or Puzzles.
